## Comparability note

Alaska Air Group's FY2024 figures are **not** directly comparable to its prior years: Alaska completed the acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward [DOC-2]. Hawaiian contributed $869 million of revenue from the acquisition date through December 31, 2024 [DOC-2], so I have removed that amount from Alaska's FY2024 revenue to produce an organic (like-for-like) growth figure. Note this adjustment is only approximate on a full-year basis — it strips out ~3.5 months of Hawaiian revenue, but Alaska's FY2022 and FY2023 revenues contain no Hawaiian contribution at all [DOC-2]. The other four carriers are all calendar-year filers with no acquisition adjustment indicated [DOC-1], so their figures are directly comparable.

Adjusted Alaska FY2024 revenue: $11,735M − $869M = **$10,866M** [DOC-1][DOC-2]

## Ranking 1 — FY2023 → FY2024 revenue growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2023 | FY2024 (adj.) | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $53,717M | $57,063M | **+6.23%** |
| 2 | Delta | $58,048M | $61,643M | +6.19% |
| 3 | Southwest | $26,091M | $27,483M | +5.33% |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $10,426M | $10,866M | +4.22% |
| 5 | American | $52,788M | $54,211M | +2.70% |

Sources: [DOC-1] for all revenue figures; [DOC-2] for the Hawaiian exclusion. United and Delta are effectively tied (6.23% vs. 6.19%) — a difference of ~4 basis points.

## Ranking 2 — FY2022 → FY2024 revenue growth

| Rank | Airline | FY2022 | FY2024 (adj.) | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | United | $44,955M | $57,063M | **+26.94%** |
| 2 | Delta | $50,582M | $61,643M | +21.87% |
| 3 | Southwest | $23,814M | $27,483M | +15.41% |
| 4 | Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) | $9,646M | $10,866M | +12.65% |
| 5 | American | $48,971M | $54,211M | +10.70% |

Sources: [DOC-1] for all revenue figures; [DOC-2] for the Hawaiian exclusion.

## Conclusion

Yes — **United Airlines Holdings ranks first in both rankings**, though its lead over Delta in the one-year ranking is within rounding-level significance (6.23% vs. 6.19%), while its two-year lead is decisive (+26.9% vs. +21.9%). The full ordering is identical across both periods: United, Delta, Southwest, Alaska, American. (Note: on an unadjusted basis Alaska's FY2023→FY2024 growth would be +12.56% and FY2022→FY2024 +21.66%, which would move it to first and third respectively — illustrating that the Hawaiian acquisition drives nearly all of Alaska's reported growth [DOC-1][DOC-2].)

ANSWER: FY23→FY24: 1. United +6.23%, 2. Delta +6.19%, 3. Southwest +5.33%, 4. Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) +4.22%, 5. American +2.70%. FY22→FY24: 1. United +26.94%, 2. Delta +21.87%, 3. Southwest +15.41%, 4. Alaska (ex-Hawaiian) +12.65%, 5. American +10.70%. Yes — United is top-ranked in both.
